analysis.title: The SMID Point
key_insights: Cactus (WHD) 3Q: revenue in line to soft, but Spoolables margin benefited from record international shipments and bookings. Pressure Control saw tailwinds from synergies, cost control and strong domestic performance.

Cactus announced a new Middle East Spoolables manufacturing plant, operational start in 2029, for $100mm in capex mostly across 2027 and 2028. Citi sees it as a local footprint in an underpenetrated market with significant growth potential.
Cactus management expects higher 3Q demand in Pressure Control to translate into defendable market share gains into 2027. Citi rates WHD Neutral, target $74.
CSW Industrials 2Q27 adj. EBITDA was $96.7mn, slightly below Citi's pre-print estimate of $97.7mn. Both Contractor Solutions and Specialized Reliability Solutions grew organically at double digits.

CSW margin strength in Specialized Reliability Solutions appears sustainable per management. Investor focus is expected to stay on the timing of margin recovery in Contractor Solutions, where freight, diesel and other input costs are outpacing pricing realization.

Citi cut CSW FY27/FY28E adj. EBITDA to $344mn/$364mn (from $346mn/$368mn), adj. EPS to $12.45/$12.85 (from $12.50/$12.90) and the EV/EBITDA multiple to 17.5x (from 18x). Target price falls to $326 from $340, rating Neutral.

Upwork 3Q beat expectations on GSV, revenue and EBITDA, but 4Q revenue and EBITDA guidance came in modestly below FactSet consensus. The marketplace faces AI automation and search-discovery headwinds.

Upwork growth initiatives: Business Plus GSV grew 132% Y/Y and is 8% of total GSV. MCP activity reached nearly 50M AI-agent requests with a $3M+ annualized Connects revenue run-rate. Lifted expects 30%+ growth in 2026 after the WorkMotion acquisition.

Upwork active clients fell to 717K (-10% Y/Y) while GSV per active client rose 8% Y/Y. Citi projects GSV pressure through 2027 and wants more visibility before turning constructive. Maintains Neutral/High Risk, target $10.50.
Citi's new Upwork 2027E estimates: GSV $3,510mn (old $3,777mn), revenue $721.5mn (old $781.3mn), adj. EBITDA $210.9mn (old $257.1mn). 2028E: GSV $3,563mn, revenue $756.0mn, adj. EBITDA $243.3mn.
At TCT, Edwards Lifesciences published PROGRESS data that Citi says validates TAVR for moderate aortic stenosis, plus strong CLASP II TR data for the PASCAL tricuspid repair device.

Citi says an existing NCD (national coverage determination) leaves language room for CMS to cover moderate AS. With the data, this should support the higher end of Edwards' mid-to-high-single-digit TAVR growth forecast for 2027+.
Boston Scientific's SIMPLAAFY RCT results were encouraging and should benefit Watchman utilization. Citi rates EW Buy and BSX Neutral.

Oil and gas equipment: behind-the-meter (BTM) power players were nearly universally bullish at Citi's August energy conference that new projects would be announced by year-end. SEI announced its largest contract to date last Thursday, a 15-year, 900MW power generation supply deal.

Citi expects two more near-term projects from Williams (longer tenures, likely geographic diversification). Atlas secured a backstop agreement from a frontier AI lab and a bridge loan. LBRT forecasts its first power contract by year-end, supported by a forthcoming prepayment.
Sentiment on the BTM power theme has soured. Citi believes the recent pullback is an opportunity to reengage with companies riding this growth wave.
